pm_exper_user_1605_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I stop feeling so nervous when I have to read something out loud in class?
pm_exper_user_1605_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) If you start to feel nervous because you think someone might joke about your words, try looking at a friendly face in the room while you read. Practicing at home with short parts of the story can make you more confident. Even if others say things, it doesn’t mean your reading isn’t good.
(b) Sometimes you might remember when kids made fun of you before, and that can make reading scary. You can tell your teacher quietly before it’s your turn so they can support you. Taking a slow breath before each sentence can help you feel steadier.
(c) It can feel hard when you have to read in front of everyone, but try to focus on the story, not the people watching. Practicing with a family member or friend can make you feel more ready. Remember, it’s fine to take your time and read at your own pace.
(d) It can feel hard when you remember times other kids laughed about how you talk, but try to focus on your own reading, not them. You can practice with someone you trust, like your mom or sister, so you feel ready before class. Remember, the way you speak is part of you, and it’s okay to take your time.

If you still want help with handling nervousness when family puts you on the spot in conversation (in any language or situation), here are some general ideas you can use:

- **Pause and breathe:** Give yourself a moment before responding. A brief pause can calm your mind and slow your heart rate.
- **Acknowledge the question:** You can say something like “Hmm, let me think” to signal you’re considering your reply — this buys you time.
- **Redirect gently:** If you’re caught off guard, you might shift the topic to something you’re more comfortable with: “That reminds me of…” or “Speaking of…”
- **Prepare phrases in advance:** Think of a few go-to responses for common topics so you have them ready when needed.
- **Use humor or lightness:** Sometimes a small joke or smile can ease the tension and help you feel more in control.
- **Set boundaries if needed:** If on-the-spot questions make you uncomfortable, it’s okay to calmly say: “I’d like to come back to that later.”
